title: Reporting Income Changes on a Veterans Pension Award
content:
Every change in a household income source must be reported to VA on a Veterans Pension award, and the veteran may report it by telephone, online or by mail.

## How the change moves the rate

**Income decrease.** An income decrease raises the rate from the first day of the month after the month the change began, and the higher amount for months already paid is released as a retroactive payment.

**Income increase.** An income increase lowers the rate effective the last day of the month in which the change began, and the lower rate is paid from the following month. When months at the old higher rate have already been paid, the adjustment records an overpayment equal to the difference between the old and new monthly amounts for each such month, and a Veterans Pension Overpayment debt is established. The months counted are the monthly payments on the award, from the first entitlement month paid at the new rate under that adjustment's effective date through the most recent monthly payment, whose gross amount exceeds the adjusted monthly rate.

**No pension left.** When the new countable income leaves no pension payable, the award is terminated for excess income.

## Decrease and increase side by side

| | Income decrease | Income increase |
|---|---|---|
| Effect on rate | raises it | lowers it |
| Effective | first day of the month after the month the change began | last day of the month in which the change began |
| Months already paid | higher amount released as a retroactive payment | overpayment for each month paid above the new monthly amount; Veterans Pension Overpayment debt established |

## Worked examples (hypothetical)

- *Decrease.* A veteran's annuity stopped in May. The higher rate is effective June 1; if June and July were already paid at the old rate of 600 and the new monthly rate is 750, the retroactive payment covers 150 for each of the two months, 300 in all.
- *Increase.* A spouse began wages in May. The lower rate is effective May 31 and paid from June. If June, July and August were already paid at 900 and the new monthly rate is 700, three months exceed the new rate and the overpayment is 200 for each, 600 in all, established as a Veterans Pension Overpayment debt.
